facts.fact: The first computer virus, 'Creeper', was created in 1971 and displayed the message: 'I'm the creeper: catch me if you can!'
About 2.5 quintillion bytes of data are created every day. That's 2,500,000,000,000,000 bytes!
The term 'phishing' was first used in 1995 and derives from 'fishing' – cybercriminals cast out bait to catch unwary internet users.
80% of cyber attacks are successful due to weak passwords. A strong password should have 12+ characters with mixed case, numbers, and symbols.
The average time to detect a data breach is 207 days. Early detection can save millions in damages.
SSH (Secure Shell) was created in 1995 as a secure alternative to Telnet and rlogin protocols which sent credentials in plain text.
A vulnerability in an unpatched Windows system can be exploited within minutes of public disclosure.
The Morris Worm of 1988 infected an estimated 6,000 computers (10% of the internet at the time) causing $10-100 million in damages.
Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) can block 99.9% of account compromise attacks, even if your password is stolen.
The CIA Triad (Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability) is the foundation of cybersecurity principles and guides all security frameworks.
SQL Injection attacks exploit improper input validation in web applications, allowing attackers to manipulate database queries.
Ransomware attacks cost businesses an average of $20,000+ per incident, with some enterprise attacks reaching millions.
The OWASP Top 10 is a regularly updated list of the most critical web application security risks every developer should know.
A single exposed database with inadequate authentication can compromise millions of users' personal data in seconds.
CTF (Capture The Flag) competitions are legal environments for practicing hacking and defensive security skills.
